items.name: Elara's Doll
items.in_room: At the foot of the largest oak, half pressed into the leaf mould, there is a rag doll with a stitched face.
items.description: Homemade, well-loved, and dry — which it should not be, after three days of rain under an open sky.
items.on_take:
You lift it and the leaf mould comes away in a neat disc, the way turned earth does. The doll is dry. Three days of rain have fallen on this grove and not one of them has touched it.

The scored bark above you is at the height of a grown man's eye. The marks were made from inside the ring, facing out.

items.name: The Bloodstone Geode
items.in_room: The veins converge on a hollow in the rock the size of a cart, and the hollow is not empty.
items.description: A geode taller than a man, its interior crowded with red crystal. The warmth in the workings comes from here. So does the grain in every wall you have passed.
items.on_destroy:
It takes longer than it should, and it does not shatter so much as give up. The red goes out of the crystal from the centre outward, and the warmth goes with it.

Somewhere above, in the palace district, a great many lamps gutter at once and then steady. The veins in the walls around you are grey now, and they are only rock.

items.name: The Undertaker's Ledger
items.in_room: A burial ledger sits among the unclaimed commissions, open at this week's page.
items.description: Four entries this week in a town that usually manages one a month. Against each, in a different hand from the undertaker's, a small mark.
items.on_take: You take the ledger. The four marks are identical, and they are not a religious sign. Whoever made them did it after the entries were written, and did it in a hurry.

items.name: A Bundle of Sacking
items.in_room: On the swept millstone lies a bundle of sacking about the size of a sleeping child, tied off with red cord.
items.description: Sacking, red cord, and a shape that is very nearly right.
items.on_take:
It is heavy the wrong way. You cut the cord and river stones spill across the millstone, and among them a strip of red cloth knotted the way the Covenant knots it.

Nobody carried a child down this road. Somebody wanted you to believe they had, and wanted you a long way from the Whisperwood while you believed it.

From back up the causeway, faint across the water, a bell begins to ring.

items.name: A Letter Under Black Wax
items.in_room: One of the kneelers left a courier's satchel by the mats. The flap is open, and there is a letter in it under a black wax seal.
items.description: Heavy cream paper. The wax carries the royal cipher.
items.on_take:
It is addressed to the keepers of the vault, and it is short.

'Keep them below as long as they are willing to stay. Hale has done well; see that the girl is kept comfortable, and remind him of her if he wavers. — L.'

The seal on the wall is painted plaster. Close enough to read by, you can see the brush strokes. Above you, the stair you came down is full of small sounds, and all of them are coming this way.

items.name: A String of Name-Tokens
items.in_room: Where the thralls fell, a length of twine lies in the leaf litter, threaded with small carved tokens.
items.description: Eleven tokens of whittled ash on garden twine, each carved with a name in a careful hand: Tessaly. Orrin. Beck. Hal. The kind a family hangs over its door for luck.
items.on_take: You wind the twine round your hand. Somebody in the valley made these, one for each of them, and somebody else went round and took them all off the doors.

items.name: A Drowning-Stone
items.in_room: One of the stones the drowned came up with has come loose from its rope and lies in the shallows, squared off and far too regular to be anything the mere made.
items.description: A cut block of grey stone the size of a loaf, with an iron ring leaded into the top and a mark chiselled into one face: a tower over three lines of water.
items.on_take: It is heavier than it looks. The mark is old, and somebody has cleaned the moss out of it recently, as if to be sure it could still be read.

items.name: The Shift's Tallies
items.in_room: The miners' brass tally-tokens lie where they fell, still on their strings.
items.description: Nine brass tokens stamped with numbers, one for each man who went down on the last shift. The foreman hands them out at the top of the shaft and takes them back at the end, and that is how he knows who is still below.
items.on_take: Nine. You count them twice. It seems important.

items.name: The Gatehouse Door
items.in_room: The gatehouse beside the gates has a door of iron-bound oak, and no handle on the outside.
items.description: Heavy, locked, and newer than the gatehouse. Somebody behind it is being very quiet on purpose.
items.on_destroy: It takes a long time, and nobody inside makes a sound until it gives. Then there are eleven of them in the doorway, blinking: servants' children, a clerk's wife, a boy in a choir tunic, and a girl of about eleven with ink on her fingers, who asks before anything else whether you have come from the library.

items.name: A Reader's Day-Book
items.in_room: One of the Readers had a day-book in its coat, the pages gone soft with damp.
items.description: An archivist's day-book, kept in a small upright hand until about a year ago, when the entries stop. The last one reads: "Sent below to catalogue the sealed stacks. Hale says a fortnight."
items.on_take: The name inside the cover is Pell Aubery, Under-Archivist. There are four more names on the flyleaf, crossed through one at a time in a different ink.
